title: MXR triangular inversion for Qwen3.6 on Ascend

paper.title: Fast and Stable Triangular Inversion for Delta-Rule Linear Transformers

objective: Reproduce the official MXR/PTO mechanism faithfully on Ascend, prove multi-step numerical correctness and target-shape advantage, then obtain attributable matched end-to-end performance without quality regression through a plugin-owned monkeypatch.

goal_alignment.long_term: Deliver reproducible and portable Ascend performance benefit through a plugin-owned implementation without modifying upstream frameworks or images.
goal_alignment.medium_term: Build a complete evidence chain: official-method parity, CANN 9.1 compatibility, NPU numerical correctness, target-shape kernel timing, matched dense end-to-end A/B, and final quality.
goal_alignment.short_term: Finish source/license/runtime audit and one-shot NPU gate preparation while NPU4-7 are occupied by an external service.

fixed_gates.stop_rule: Stop heavy integration and move to KVBuffer if the candidate has no clear target-shape kernel advantage or the attributable end-to-end gain is expected to remain below about 5 percent.

next_actions: Freeze an executable target-shape numerical and timing contract for H=12, Hg=4, D=128, chunk=128.
Prepare a fail-closed NPU4-7 controller with immutable artifact root and no automatic retries.
When a target card is truly idle, run one compile plus numerical gate before any timing.
If the gate passes, compare official staged, official megakernel, and the v0.23 baseline on the same target shape; preserve attribution between triangular inversion and full fusion.
Only integrate the winning path into vLLM after the target-shape gate passes.
